subject: Re: Temporary subprocessor waiver request — runtime telemetry to analytics partner
messages:
From: Dana Myers <dana@healthsync.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Miguel Torres <miguel@analytica.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary subprocessor waiver request for analytics pilot

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency and cost numbers look promising. We have a short internal ask: our compliance team requires that any vendor subprocessing our telemetry for pilot analytics be explicitly permitted in the DPA. Analytica (Miguel copied) is a one-off analytics partner we'll use for a 6‑week pilot and they need access to aggregated runtime telemetry only (no raw user prompts or model outputs).

Is Redwood willing to accept a temporary waiver / amendment that: 
- Allows Analytica as a named subprocessor for the pilot period (6 weeks)
- Restricts processing to aggregated telemetry metrics and error traces (attached scope spreadsheet)
- Requires deletion of any transient KV cache snapshots and any association with customer identifiers within 14 days of ingestion

I attached a short waiver request doc. Can you route this to legal and security and let us know whether your product team needs any runtime changes to support the constraint on export-only aggregated telemetry? We’re on a tight timeline to get the pilot running April 2.

Appreciate your help — Dana

Attachments: HealthSync_Waiver_Request.pdf
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Dana Myers <dana@healthsync.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary subprocessor waiver request for analytics pilot

Dana — thanks for the clear ask and the attachment. Looping in Product (Dev) and Security/Legal (Rishi/Olga) for technical feasibility and a redline.

Quick product note: we can export aggregated telemetry (token counts, tail latency distributions, error rates, model selection metrics) without exporting prompt or output text. However, a few operational items to confirm before we can sign off: 
- Where will Analytica ingest the telemetry? (S3 in us-west vs. their managed endpoint)
- We’ll need a short-term subproc entry and an export job with a strict sampling/config to ensure no PII by accident
- KV cache snapshots are not part of our standard telemetry pipeline but there are edge-case debug snapshots we’d need to ensure aren’t exported

Olga/Rishi — can Legal/Security take a look and propose redline language for a 6‑week limited subprocessor entry + deletion SLA? Dev, can you estimate whether any config flag or a temporary export-only policy is needed and how long to implement?

Irene

--
Irene Choi
Head of Product Security Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Dana Myers <dana@healthsync.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Mar 2028 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary subprocessor waiver request for analytics pilot

Hi all,

Technical feasibility update: we can support the pilot with configuration only — no runtime code change required if the requirement is strictly aggregated metrics (we already emit metrics via our telemetry exporter). Implementation plan: 
- Create an export job scoped to HealthSync -> Analytica S3 bucket (or secure HTTPS endpoint) with schema limited to: model_id, bucketed latency p50/p95/p99, token_counts (binned), error_code, inference_timestamp. No prompt/output fields will be present.
- Add a production-only sampling rule to avoid exporting any request-level trace that includes user metadata.
- Add a one-time verification run to assert no PII fields are present (running on a synthetic sample).
- To satisfy deletion SLA: retention rule on the target bucket + signed attestation from Analytica on deletion within 14 days.

Estimate: 3 business days to configure and validate if Analytica can accept S3; 5 business days if they require a custom endpoint and we do connectivity testing.

Dev

--
Dev Patel
Senior Product Manager, Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Dana Myers <dana@healthsync.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Mar 2028 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft redline for limited subprocessor entry (6-week pilot)

Dana / Irene — attaching a draft redline of the DPA that adds a limited subprocessor entry for Analytica constrained to aggregated telemetry. Key points addressed in the draft: 
- Narrow subprocessor scope: explicitly enumerates allowed telemetry fields and prohibits transfer of raw prompts, outputs, or user identifiers. 
- Timebox: 6-week pilot window with automatic expiry; any extension requires written approval.
- Deletion & proof: Analytica must delete ingested telemetry within 14 days of ingestion and provide deletion logs/evidence (hashes/timestamps) within 21 days of request.
- Audit rights: Redwood reserves the right to conduct a remote compliance check during the pilot; Analytica must provide evidence of secure storage and access controls.
- Liability carveouts limited to the scope of aggregated telemetry only.

A few asks to HealthSync: confirm whether Analytica will accept a signed attestation + S3 lifecycle policy as deletion proof, or whether you need us to require a signed audit report from Analytica. Also, we need to know the destination for exports to confirm access controls.

Attachment: redline_dpa_healthsync.docx

Olga Petrov
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Dana Myers <dana@healthsync.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Mar 2028 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary subprocessor waiver request for analytics pilot — product & security signoff

Thanks everyone — reading the draft now and appreciate the close scope. Quick internal signoffs: 
- Product (Dev): signoff to proceed with configuration path; 3 business days to stand up and validate S3 export + sampling rules.
- Security (Rishi): conditional signoff provided we add the remote compliance check and require deletion logs (Olga to own language).
- Legal (Olga): redline attached and ready for HealthSync review — please confirm acceptance of deletion proof by attestation + S3 lifecycle policy.

Dana — from Redwood’s side this is approvable once you confirm destination and Analytica’s deletion proof approach. If you confirm S3 + attestation we can get this live by March 29 (assuming HealthSync returns signed amendment and Analytica test bucket is provisioned).

Next steps (short):
1) HealthSync confirms destination + deletion proof approach (reply to this thread)
2) HealthSync signs amendment (Olga to send final DocuSign link)
3) Dev validates export and runs one verification pass

I’ll mark this as approved for the pilot contingent on those items.

Thanks — Irene

--
Irene Choi
Head of Product Security Operations
Redwood Inference
